candidates.title: How you can improve your memory
candidates.evidence: Direct page opened; substantive article with expert review and sections on encoding, consolidation, transfer limits, practice and extraordinary memory.

candidates.title: Working Out to Stay Sharp
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed a current full NIH article explaining exercise and brain health with concrete advice.
candidates.decision: Good official health input, but broader behavior advice and exercise claims would need more medical-scope caveats than the chosen reading.

candidates.title: Food and Feasting at Stonehenge
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed a substantive official page combining daily diet, feasting, travel, cooking and isotope evidence.
candidates.decision: Strong candidate, rejected because archaeology and interpretation were too close to the immediately preceding public-history lesson.

candidates.title: Science Misinformation
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed an official guide on identifying science misinformation and source signals.
candidates.decision: Useful but too close to the recent sequence of evidence-strength and source-audit lessons.

candidates.title: How (and why) to unboil an egg
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed a real Academy article on the chemistry and practical significance of protein refolding.
candidates.decision: Real and engaging, but narrower food-chemistry value and weaker general-language transfer than the selected article.

candidates.title: How does science work?
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed a long Academy explainer on evidence, measurement, publication and peer review.
candidates.decision: High-quality explainer, rejected because scientific-method/evidence framing has appeared repeatedly in the last week.

candidates.title: Objects Conservation Practice at The Met
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed a detailed institutional essay on examination, imaging, environmental control and treatment decisions.
candidates.decision: Substantive but longer and thematically close to preservation and historical interpretation.

candidates.title: Ocean pollution and marine debris
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed an official resource page explaining sources, impacts, monitoring and public decisions.
candidates.decision: Official source, but the page is organized primarily as a resource collection and is less cohesive as a 5–15 minute single input.

candidates.title: The Role of Inventions in Changing Our Daily Lives
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed a real LOC teaching article on how inventions alter jobs, technology and everyday life.
candidates.decision: Real LOC article, rejected because invention-driven social change overlaps the 2026-10-26 photocopier lesson.

candidates.title: History of the autochrome
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed a detailed museum article on colour-screen grains, exposure limits and documentary uses.
candidates.decision: Strong museum article, but photography/visual-media history is too close to the 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27 topics.

candidates.title: How our memory develops
candidates.evidence: Search observation showed a real Academy article on changes in memory across development.
candidates.decision: Real source but semantic/topic duplicate within this candidate pool and same publisher; permanently excluded for this operation once the selected memory article won.
